name: Seedai
subtitle: small rice flour spheres fried crisp for Krishna Jayanthi
prepNotes: Seedai has a reputation for bursting in the oil. Two things cause it: air pockets in the balls and undissolved salt.
Dissolve the salt in the water before it touches the flour, and roll each ball smooth with no cracks.

steps.text: Sieve the flours together. Dissolve the salt and asafoetida in a little water and add that, not dry salt.
steps.tip: Undissolved salt crystals are the classic cause of a seedai exploding.

steps.text: Rub in the butter and coconut, then bring together into a stiff dough with water.
Roll small marble-sized balls, keeping each one completely smooth with no cracks.
steps.tip: A crack is where the steam gets in. Roll them properly.

steps.text: Spread the balls on a cloth and air-dry 20 minutes.
Fry a small batch on medium first as a test. If it holds, fry the rest until the bubbling stops.
steps.tip: Test batch first, and stand back from the pan for the first minute.

storage: Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight tin at room temperature. The coconut is what limits it; beyond that it can turn.
